book.title: Rest: Why You Get More Done When You Work Less
book.author: Alex Soojung-Kim Pang

confidence_note: About four hours of focused work a day, Darwin as Pang's lead example, and the Sandwalk as an example of deliberate rest are confirmed from several secondary sources; the specific times and household details (sofa, Emma reading, The Times, backgammon, bed at ten thirty) come from a biographical schedule (Aydon) that Pang's account is consistent with, but the book text was not read. Old-text work block 8:00 to 10:30, and the list of Hemingway, Beethoven, Beauvoir, Dickens as all working four to five hours, and 'always superior' claim were dropped as unverified or wrong.
facts: Pang uses Darwin as the main example of a creative worker with about four hours of focused work a day.
Darwin started in his study after eight, worked about ninety minutes, then rested about an hour on a sofa while his wife Emma read to him, then worked about ninety minutes more.
Around midday he took his main walk on the Sandwalk, a gravel path about a quarter mile long at the back of his garden; Pang treats it as an example of deliberate rest.
Lunch with the family at one, then rest on the sofa reading The Times, then letters.
Another rest and walk, then about an hour of work in the late afternoon.
Evening: supper, Emma played piano, a game of backgammon, bed at ten thirty.
Caveat: critics say four hours understates his total scientific work and one routine does not prove four hours is ideal for every profession.
tension: A day with four work hours produced a body of work.
opening_idea: The day Pang reads in Darwin's schedule.

lessons.idea: Plan hard work in short blocks with real breaks.
lessons.anchor: Darwin's ninety-minute blocks separated by sofa and walk.
lessons.everyday_example_idea: A translator works in two blocks with a walk between.

reflect_final: Which hours of your day are actually good for demanding work, and what do you do between them to recover?

use_cases.move: Block ninety minutes for the hardest task, then a walk, like Darwin's Sandwalk.

use_cases.situation: Partner wants you to keep working
use_cases.move: Say you will stop and take a walk and be back.

pocket_idea: Ninety minutes of hard work, then a walk: Darwin's day ran on blocks and breaks.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Darwin worked about four hours a day.
